caption: Some months it's R13 000, some months it's this. Losing one household for two weeks is the whole difference. Whose income changes just as much as mine?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R9 800
p/m income
Living in Kuruman
slides.body:
Female, 44
Married, three kids (16, 12, 8)
Job: Domestic worker, cleans for three households on different days
Net income: R9 800 p/m (this month)

slides.title: Taxi fare
slides.includes: Two taxis each way, all three households across town
slides.body: Some weeks the taxi costs more than what one of the households pays me that week.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Staples, plus what I pick up on the way home
slides.body: My husband covers the rest. This is just what comes from my side.

slides.title: School uniforms & stationery
slides.includes: Saving toward three sets of school shoes before December
slides.body: I put a little aside every payout so January doesn't wreck us.

slides.title: Stokvel
slides.includes: With the other domestic workers on the same street
slides.body: We've never missed a month between the six of us.

slides.title: Funeral policy
slides.includes: My own, plus a small top-up for my mother
slides.body: The one thing I'd go without groceries before I'd cancel.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Airtime & data, electricity contribution, clothing account, my mother's support, taxi fare to church
slides.body: Small things, but on this income there's no such thing as a small thing.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R9 800 this month. Some months it's closer to R13 000 when nobody cancels. This was one of the thin ones.

slides.title: I stopped guessing between the good weeks and the thin ones
slides.body:
I upload my statement to Beyond Horizon whenever a job pays out, even the small ones.

Seeing the thin months next to the good ones finally made sense of why some Decembers feel impossible.

No bank login needed.
